topics.topic: Runtime environment-table item schema and whether setting normalization preserves exact text
questions: What metadata does the closed environment table hold for each item: type and normalization, type and requiredness and normalization, or only type and field mapping?
Does runtime_settings preserve every environment value byte-for-byte as text, or does it perform a hidden per-item normalization?
Which attributes does the closed environment table own for each item, and does runtime_settings perform any normalization or only return the exact optional text value?
What fields does each environment-table item actually carry, and what does “whether it is its normalization” mean?

Is normalization an identity operation that preserves the environment text exactly, or may `runtime_settings` transform a set value despite saying every item is taken as set with no trimming, case or Unicode normalization?

quotes:
Every item is text taken as it is set: no
trimming, no case or Unicode normalization;
Environment reading and the per-item normalization.
judgement.divergence: runtime_settings either preserves leading and trailing spaces exactly or applies a per-item normalization that changes them; configuration and the owner notice which store path is checked and opened.
judgement.why: The text simultaneously says that no normalization occurs and that runtime_settings hides per-item normalization.

bases.passage:
Every item is text taken as it is set: no
trimming, no case or Unicode normalization;
Environment reading and the per-item normalization.

unsupported_sides:
Every item is text taken as it is set: no
trimming, no case or Unicode normalization;
Environment reading and the per-item normalization.

witness.initial: REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION is set to ` /srv/registry.db ` with leading and trailing spaces, and every other item is valid.
events: configuration checks the resulting store location.
outcomes: runtime_settings preserves the spaces, so configuration checks and resolves the path ` /srv/registry.db `.
runtime_settings applies its hidden per-item normalization, so configuration checks and resolves a different path such as `/srv/registry.db`.
witness.observer: configuration and the owner starting Registry
basis:
It checks nothing: it answers each item as
set, or absent.

The path checks of rule 5 that need no file — the store and
the backup location apart, compared with every link resolved — are its too.

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2);

topics.topic: Scope and orchestration ownership of A17 startup checks
questions: Does configuration own and orchestrate every A17 rule 2 start check, including the backup probe and store opening, or only the pure checks that precede those delegated checks?

Does configuration own and orchestrate every A17 rule 2 startup check, including the backup probe, store opening or creation, and listener opening, or does it own only the checks that its Must not own section permits?

Does `configuration` own every check in A17 rule 2, including the backup probe, store opening or creation, and listener opening, or only the pure presence, form, secret and path-comparison checks listed here while `backups`, `store` and another lifecycle module own the effectful checks?

quotes:
A17: every start check of rule 2, in its one order, over the settings
`runtime_settings` loads as set — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value; that no default is applied (rule 5); an owner-only start when no token
is given (rule 1).

Reading the environment (`runtime_settings`), opening or making the store
(`store`), probing the backup location (`backups`), what a token may do
(`service_access`), the credential check of a sign-in (`owner_sessions`).
judgement.divergence: On an unwritable backup location, load_configuration either owns the probe and returns its failure, or returns successfully after the pure configuration checks and instance_lifecycle obtains the failure from backups; instance_lifecycle and module tests observe the different owner and call path.
judgement.why: configuration is assigned every A17 rule 2 check while its Must not own passage assigns the backup probe and store opening to other modules.

bases.passage:
A17: every start check of rule 2, in its one order, over the settings
`runtime_settings` loads as set — the service tokens of the services
`data_provider`'s rights table lists, all or none, the other items present,
each well formed, each secret at least the 32 bytes `data_provider` holds, no
two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its
value; that no default is applied (rule 5); an owner-only start when no token
is given (rule 1).
bases.rests_on:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).

bases.passage:
Reading the environment (`runtime_settings`), opening or making the store
(`store`), probing the backup location (`backups`), what a token may do
(`service_access`), the credential check of a sign-in (`owner_sessions`).

unsupported_sides:
Reading the environment (`runtime_settings`), opening or making the store
(`store`), probing the backup location (`backups`), what a token may do
(`service_access`), the credential check of a sign-in (`owner_sessions`).

witness.initial: All presence, form, secret and path-comparison checks pass, but the configured backup location is not writable.
events: The ordered startup reaches the backup-location probe.
outcomes: configuration owns every A17 rule 2 check, invokes the probe as part of load_configuration and returns the failed-start diagnostic.
configuration owns only the pure checks, returns a loaded configuration, and instance_lifecycle then calls backups for the probe and receives the failed-start diagnostic.
witness.observer: instance_lifecycle, its callers, and module-level tests
basis:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the release's addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2);

A18: the daily run at 03:00 UTC while Registry runs with its tokens, from the
minute look and the dates the process remembers (rule 1); the copy, without
agent sessions, that `store` writes at the temporary path `backups` names
(rule 2), encrypted with the configured key, recording its
instant, release, last sequence number and key digest (rules 1, 3); the three
steps — removing temporary files, writing and checking the backup by
decrypting it and asking `store` to check the copy, deleting backups older
than 30 × 24 hours and unreadable ones (rule 4); the prefixes and the location
rules (rule 5), the probe file of A17 rule 2; the newest kept backup's instant
for the owner interface. No run in an owner-only start (rule 9).

topics.topic: Upload handoff path and ownership of upload size and readability decisions
questions: Through which declared dependency does owner_interface hand the declared length and unread stream to migration_import, since owner_interface knows operations but not migration_import?

Through which module does owner_interface hand off the declared length and unread stream, and does “operations decides” mean operations owns the A19 size-limit decision or merely coordinates migration_import's decision?

For an upload, does `operations` decide the declared-length, actual-byte-limit and unreadable-stream checks, or does `migration_import` decide them as its ownership passage and the preceding owner-interface passage say?
Does `owner_interface` hand the upload directly to `migration_import`, requiring a dependency absent from its Knows list, or hand it to `operations`, which then calls `migration_import`?

quotes:
`module:operations`. Run one owner request: sign-in and sign-out, the
confirmation step, the upload and the mapping, and every owner action in
its one transaction with its entry and confirmation id (A04, A13, A14, A16).

The compositions: an erasure with `agent_sessions.drop_project_from_sessions`
and, deleting whole, `artifact_pointers.delete_pointers_of_project`; a grant
through a request with `projects.validate_project_reference`; the import
through `migration_import`, closed by `record_migration_closure`, then
`owner_sessions.drop_uploaded_files`.

`module:migration_import`. Read an uploaded export file as data and answer
its projects, or, for the owner's picks, the mapping (A16 rules 1, 3–5).

The read transaction; the mode, `upload` or `mapping`; at `upload`, the
request's declared length, or that it declared none, and its unread byte
stream, which this operation reads at most one byte past the imported
`IMPORT_FILE_MAX_BYTES` constant; at `mapping`, the kept file's bytes;
judgement.why: State 5 fixes the handoff as owner_interface calling operations, which coordinates the import by calling migration_import; migration_import receives the declared length and unread stream and applies the size and readability checks.

topics.topic: Dependency path for migration import to receive the operations-owned transaction and confirmation id
questions: How can migration_import use the transaction and confirmation id owned by operations when operations is absent from its Knows list: does operations call migration_import and pass them in, or may migration_import depend on operations and request them?

topics.topic: Interpretation and handoff value for absent or invalid declared upload length
questions: What value is handed on when the request has no declared length or has a declared-length header that cannot be interpreted as a non-negative byte count, and which module interprets that header?

topics.topic: Ownership split for the no-default configuration policy
questions: Which module owns the decision that no configuration item receives a default, and what distinct responsibility, if any, does the other module have?

topics.topic: Timing of the first backup polling call
questions: Does `instance_lifecycle` call `backups` immediately when the process starts and then every 60 seconds, or only after the first 60-second interval?

quotes:
the minute look's 60 seconds is one that
`instance_lifecycle` applies, calling `backups` at that interval.
judgement.why: Whether the recurring backup flow performs its first call immediately or after one interval is flow timing, owned by State 4 rather than State 3's module ownership and dependency boundary.
